findings.place: End of the heading, after topologique
findings.evidence: The single title crop shows an isolated pale grey oblique dot just beyond the final letter, below its terminal. Its density is much lower than the main title ink; punctuation status remains open. The main title and complete long descenders are inside the crop.
findings.h_marking_detail: No title terminal punctuation is transcribed in H.

findings.evidence: After the tall crossed t, the ending has a low attached return and one short detached terminal curl, with a high mark above the compressed group. Two separate final e bodies cannot be isolated with confidence. The crop retains both written candidates; grammatical agreement with paire did not decide it.

findings.place: Parenthesis after une paire: indiciellement, split across two manuscript lines
findings.evidence: The crop gives the dotted initial i, low n, tall returning d, dotted i/c/i sequence, two tall looped l strokes, and the continuation -ment on the short line underneath. The final t has its tall stroke and return. The line-end break is joined in the transcription.

findings.mathematical_note: The transition from the cancelled ensembles to parties did not supply or erase the accent.
findings.place: Before the cancelled ensembles and replacement parties
findings.evidence: The crop shows d followed by a separate rounded e. A short detached rising stroke sits directly over that e. Its placement supports the written accent in dé; there is no separately placed apostrophe between d and the e. The unchanged high stroke is retained despite the syntax after the correction.

findings.confidence: low for earlier glyph; high for visible overwriting
findings.mathematical_note: The displayed distinctness statement does not decide the identity of the older crossed capital.
findings.place: First capital of display (3), underlying crossed strokes
findings.evidence: Under the live angular Sigma are two crossing diagonals and additional central/basal returns. The top and bottom Sigma bars remain readable. The combined marks support an earlier X or an earlier Sigma, but a complete earlier letter and the exact cancellation operation are not separately exposed. Uncertainty therefore covers both the older identity and its state, immediately before the live replacement.

findings.confidence: low for earlier state; high for live inequality
findings.mathematical_note: Distinctes and the other written inequalities were contextual cues, but they were not used to choose an earlier sign.
findings.evidence: The crop shows two horizontal bars, a heavy near-upright crossing descending below them, and a dense right-hand knot. The live not-equal mark is clear. The layered bars do not isolate an older crossing, so an earlier = or an earlier not-equal remains open; separate prior cancellation versus reinforcement remains open as well.

findings.mathematical_note: The epsilon-prime earlier in this same displayed condition was used as a letterform comparison; expected index meaning alone was not used.
findings.place: Last primed index in the condition at the right of display (3)
findings.evidence: The final letter has the same hooked upper arc and returning lower bend as the immediately preceding primed epsilon in the list epsilon, epsilon-prime. Its lower terminal is shorter, but the same line supplies a directly visible shape comparison. The separated high prime is clear.

findings.mathematical_note: The visible sequence (1), (2), (2'), and (4) was noted only as context and did not resolve the ambiguous body.
findings.place: Left label of the distinctness display
findings.evidence: Between the parentheses the body rises to a narrow angled cap, falls to the right, and returns left at its foot. A separate pair of 3 lobes is not exposed. The surrounding labels make 3 the first candidate but do not settle this shape; s and a wedge-like body remain recorded.

findings.mathematical_note: The named mathematical term did not determine the second written accent.
findings.evidence: The first accent is a detached stroke rising to the right. The second is a very short near-upright speck above the compressed final vowel group; its tilt is insufficient to choose grave versus acute. The underline is a single independent line and the plural ending is visible.

findings.place: Cancelled article between binaire, and et l'ensemble
findings.evidence: The crop exposes a tall looped l and a low closed terminal oval with overlaid right-hand strokes. That terminal permits a or e. The group is cancelled, and both candidate letters remain recoverable enough for an uncertain reading rather than an illegible-word token.

findings.mathematical_note: The written final omega within the same lower index provides the local shape comparison.
findings.place: First lower index under the intersection in (4), older layer
findings.evidence: Below the high curled epsilon there is a lower open two-hump remnant with a left upturn. The low form resembles the omega at the right of the same index. Coalescence with the live epsilon's lower stroke prevents a fully separate reconstruction of the older glyph and its overwritten state, so omega/epsilon and state uncertainty are retained.

findings.place: End of the interlinear addition in the last paragraph
findings.evidence: At the far right of the second added line the first character has a short tall d loop and a low bowl. The following low return sequence and open terminal give onc. The whole word is contained within the single coherent insertion crop. It reads donc.
findings.h_marking_detail: H's editorial note explicitly identifies the full complementary-parts phrase as interlinear; it does not mark donc as uncertain.

findings.mathematical_note: Its role as the family name does not decide capitalization.
findings.place: Family letter in the first display, recurring in (2')
findings.evidence: The first display crop shows a short common top bar, a near-straight descending left leg, and a right leg ending with an outward turn; its height is less than the adjacent Sigma. Half a shows the same shape in (2'). I use pi as first reading but preserve the capital-Pi alternative at the first occurrence because this page does not supply an independently distinct case pair.

findings.mathematical_note: The phrase describing two elements supplies context for à, but the two actual strokes retain the colon alternative.
findings.place: Abbreviation and following two-mark group in omega's parenthesis
findings.evidence: After ens the crop has one short low bent mark and one detached high point, vertically paired. No further separately spaced full stop is visible between ens and that pair. I retain à as first reading of the pair with colon as an alternative; H's additional abbreviation dot is not separately supported.

findings.mathematical_note: The word supposé refers back to the written distinctness requirement; that reference was not used to invent the auxiliary or accent.
findings.evidence: Half a, confirmed in the overlap at the top of half b, shows a separate low a after l'on and a detached high acute at the end of supposé. The verb body and its final ending were read from the ink. The past participle and separate auxiliary are kept.

findings.mathematical_note: The earlier family is indexed with epsilon. That context is recorded as a possible authorial mismatch; the superscript is transcribed as written and no correction is made.
findings.place: Upper-right superscript of Sigma in display (4)
findings.evidence: Half b already shows two low humps, and the crop of the index also contains this superscript clearly. The low horizontal two-hump shape matches the written omega at the lower right of the intersection index. H's editorial note explicitly records the written omega while its displayed formula uses epsilon.
findings.h_editorial_note: \note{dans (4) l'exposant est écrit $\omega$ au lieu de $\varepsilon$}

findings.mathematical_note: The final implication in the prose did not dictate the verb: indique is the ink reading.
findings.place: Last paragraph, verb after ce qui
findings.evidence: The tight crop shows dotted i, a low compressed n, a single tall d return with its bowl, a second i dot, and q-u-e. The earlier implique on this page has a visibly different long p/l sequence. Here the tall d body is legible. The q descender continues through the crop's lower edge; this clipping is recorded and did not obscure the decisive upper letterforms.

findings.mathematical_note: No grammatical expectation was used to settle the high mark.
findings.evidence: The cropped group before aurait begins with a small rounded rising return followed by an n-like wave. A separate tall initial l is not isolated. A tiny high point over the group leaves the segmentation open, so on is retained as first reading and l'on as alternative.

findings.mathematical_note: The grammar of the completed sentence agrees with this attachment, but the descending leader and baseline order supply the reading evidence.
findings.place: Attachment of complémentaires l'un de l'autre, donc in the final sentence
findings.c: sont \inserted{complémentaires l'un de l'autre, \unsure{donc}} à la fois
findings.h:
complémentaires
l'un de l'autre, donc sont à la fois
findings.reading: sont \inserted{complémentaires l'un de l'autre, donc} à la fois
findings.evidence: The added phrase sits on two short interlinear lines. Its broad curved leader comes down after the baseline sont and before the baseline à la fois. The baseline sont is visibly left of the leader tip. I therefore attach the addition at that location. H's note correctly identifies the group as added; the finding concerns its textual position.

notes.text: The handwritten heading reads Décompositions n-aires d'un espace topologique, followed by a doubtful pale point. Version II is written obliquely at upper left and underlined. The body begins 1.1. The light pencil 31 at bottom left is retained only as the archive-sheet comment. No manuscript date is visible.

The page introduces a binary decomposition of X as an indexed pair of distinct closed parts and writes their union as X in (1). The index is epsilon in omega, and the parenthesis describes omega using ens and deux éléments. The small two-mark group between them remains à/colon-uncertain. The family-letter case remains pi/Pi-uncertain at its first occurrence.
source_elements: Opening paragraph and parenthetic notation remark
First indexed-family display and omega parenthesis

notes.text: The author writes nonemptiness of every Sigma^epsilon in (2), then says ce qui signifie aussi que before (2'), whose family differs from {emptyset, X}. These are recorded as the author's statements. No independent equivalence proof was performed during this reading.

The following sentence explicitly contains X ≠ emptyset and card X ≥ 2, with the words puisque l'on a supposé leading to the distinctness display. The ink includes the auxiliary a and the acute of supposé. The display's label and two overwritten places remain uncertain; the final epsilon-prime was resolved by comparison with the primed epsilon earlier on that same line.
source_elements: Nonempty X, cardinality, and reference to the assumption

notes.text: The inclusion passage writes Sigma^{epsilon'} subset Sigma^epsilon and then Sigma^epsilon = X, joined by ce qui équivaut, par (1), à la relation. The reference to (1) was read as an authorial cue. The prime belongs to the left Sigma in the inclusion. I did not independently re-prove the author's equivalence.

The parts are called hémisphères, and E is called équateur. In (4) the visible superscript on Sigma is omega, while the live index under the intersection reads epsilon in omega. H explicitly notes this written omega but displays epsilon in its formula. The transcription retains omega and the uncertain older layer under the first epsilon. The term équateur has one independent underline; its long q descender and letter baseline initially made the half-image appearance crowded.
source_elements: Naming the hemispheres and introducing E

notes.text: The final paragraph discusses E = emptyset. Its verb after ce qui reads indique. The index condition and the phrase complémentaires l'un de l'autre, donc are interlinear additions. The latter's leader attaches after the baseline sont. The baseline continuation says à la fois fermés et ouverts — donc que X est disconnexe. The author does not append a question mark or a separate checking note.
source_elements: Inserted index condition in the final paragraph

notes.text: Mathematical cues used during reading were restricted to visible local comparisons: the epsilon-prime earlier in the same condition, the low omega at the end of the intersection index, the family indexed by epsilon elsewhere on this page, and the sequence of display labels. These cues were documented alongside the ink. The display-label sequence did not settle the angled (3) body, and the indexing context did not replace the written omega superscript. No proof, computation, or formal certificate was run.

check_events_explanation: No mathematical proof check, independent re-proof, computation, formal certificate, or external theorem verification was performed. The page was read and its mathematical structure followed only for transcription; that reading is not logged as a proof check.

workflow_feedback.method: Thirteen single tight crops were created only for loci still open after the one-pass half readings. Each used original-image coordinates, autocontrast, LANCZOS enlargement to 3000 pixels wide, and UnsharpMask(radius=1.0, percent=120, threshold=3). No target required rotation. Complete reading.tex was saved immediately after the last crop readings and before composing this return.

crop_notes.outcome: The doubtful double-line appearance resolved as one underline plus the written letter baseline. No collation difference.
crop_notes.bounds_note: The q descender reaches the crop's final source row 2093. A non-OCR pixel-row audit found dark pixels at x592–593 there and no dark continuation in source rows 2094–2095 within the crop's x range. The decisive underline is wholly inside. No second crop was made.

crop_notes.outcome: The verb body resolves as indique.
crop_notes.bounds_note: The q descender continues beyond the crop's lower edge y2274; this was an overly short lower bound. The decisive d and i/q bodies are inside. No repeat crop was made after the reading settled. The finding bbox extends to y2320 to cover the long mark and context.
The complete target label is inside; the top border includes a partial neighbouring descender from the preceding text, which is not the target.
